title: A home at Panchavati
hookLine: an old vulture vows to guard Sita, a brother builds a hut, and the reason Rama is rarely pictured alone
carry: ram parivar: the whole family on the altar

lines: A GIANT BIRD ON A TREE.
cards: Halfway there, a huge bird settles on a tree in front of them. A vulture, enormous and old. After Viradha, Rama's first thought is a rakshasa in disguise, and he asks who it is.
The bird answers gently. I was a friend of your father, he says. My name is Jatayu.
And he offers what no one else has: when you two brothers go out into the forest, I'll stay and watch over Sita.

teach.b: Jatayu, the vulture king, gives his lineage, a long one reaching back to the beginning of creatures. Hearing he was Dasharatha's friend, Rama embraces him.
Hold on to this: of everyone in the forest book, this old bird's promise will cost the most.

Then they reach Panchavati, usually explained as the place of five banyan trees, on the Godavari, with flowering trees, deer and peacocks. Rama turns to Lakshmana: you choose the spot. Lakshmana would rather be told.
As long as you live, he says, I'm here to do what you ask.
So Rama picks a level place near the water, and Lakshmana builds the hut: walls of packed earth, bamboo posts, a roof of leaves and long grass.
Then he bathes, gathers flowers and fruit, and makes an offering for the new home.

teach.h: WITH YOU, OUR FATHER IS NOT GONE.
teach.b: Rama holds his brother and says something close to this: with you here, it's as if our father is not gone. Here's why it matters.
Walk into many Hindu homes and you'll find the Ram Darbar on the altar: Rama and Sita seated, Lakshmana standing beside them, Hanuman kneeling at their feet.
Rama is rarely shown alone. Many Hindus say the love inside his family, a wife who follows him, a brother who builds, a devotee who serves, is part of what they pray to.
They call it Ram parivar, Rama's family, and keep it as a picture of what their own home could be.

how: Panchavati is identified by many pilgrims with a site at Nashik on the Godavari, and the hut Lakshmana builds is a favorite scene in Ramayana art and performance.

o: the island city across the sea where Ravana rules
five banyans by the Godavari, where the brothers make a home
the forest hermitage where Agastya gives Rama his bow

games.q: the new home — tap the pairs.
p: Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman
builds the hut with his hands

s: on Hindu altars, Rama is usually shown alone
the Ram Darbar shows him with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman: his family is part of the prayer.
Jatayu offers to watch over Sita
when the brothers are away in the forest.
Lakshmana builds it, and Rama embraces him.

games.q: you're Lakshmana. Rama says: you choose where we'll live. what do you say?
o: ask Rama to choose, then build what he chooses.
games.why: Lakshmana asks to be told. Rama chooses, and Lakshmana builds the hut: the brother's love Hindus keep beside Rama on the altar.

practice: If your family keeps a shrine, picture it now; if not, picture the Ram Darbar: Rama and Sita seated, Lakshmana standing, Hanuman at their feet. Then add your own people, one by one, the ones who built you a place to land.
If you pray, ask a blessing for each. If you don't, breathe in thanks for each face, and breathe out ease.

wordCard.voice: Panchavati. Five banyans by the Godavari, where Lakshmana builds a hut and Rama says: with you here, our father is not gone.

orig.note: Sanskrit jaṭāyu: the old vulture king, friend of Dasharatha, who promises to guard Sita.

carryVoice: Your line: Ram parivar: the whole family on the altar. And an old bird has promised to keep watch. I'm glad you came.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 15 (Panchavati; the hut; Rama embraces Lakshmana)
